physical_harm: Lacerated wounds on the second victim, no gunshot wound
number_of_offences: Three offences charged, two counts finally upheld (Section 302 and 325 IPC)
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that a gun shot was fired at Baggar Singh which hit him in the leg, and that the post mortem report showed only lacerated wounds on the dead body of Hoshiar Singh with no gun shot wound.
witness_credibility: The court expressed doubt regarding the prosecution's version of events concerning the charge under Section 302 IPC, indicating some credibility issues with the prosecution's narrative.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 24.4.92; Trial judgment: 4.12.2006; High Court decision: 4.12.2006; Supreme Court decision: 03.02.2011
legal_representation: Rajiv Garg, Ashish Garg and Annam D.N. Rao for the Appellant; Kuldip Singh for the Respondent
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction under Section 307 IPC; High Court: Conviction under Section 302 IPC; Supreme Court: Acquitted under Section 302 IPC, convicted under Section 325 IPC read with Section 34 IPC
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that Hoshiar Singh was taken away by the accused and after 15/20 minutes gun shots were heard, leading to his death. They sought conviction under Section 302 IPC.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the post mortem report showed only lacerated wounds on the dead body of Hoshiar Singh, with no gun shot wound, creating doubt about the charge under Section 302 IPC.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle of the benefit of doubt to the accused in the absence of conclusive evidence of the charge under Section 302 IPC.
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the appellants were found guilty under Section 325 IPC read with Section 34 IPC for firing a gunshot at Baggar Singh which hit him in the leg.
other_sentence_order: The court ordered that the sentence of imprisonment imposed on the appellants shall remain suspended during the pendency of the appeal, provided each of them furnishes personal bond in the sum of Rs. 20,000/- with two sureties in the sum of Rs. 10,000/- each to the satisfaction of the trial court. Their bonds are discharged accordingly.
